limits: EL7 means the tested Oracle Linux 7.9 x86_64 target, not all RHEL/CentOS 7 machines

Configuration readback is not proof of hardware effects; live events may reassert after clearing

Windows/macOS checks validate the portable core, not a complete OS hardware backend

supplemental_local_research.scope: Eight complete original ICCmax/topology functions; synthetic MSR/container boundaries only. The ninth pinned function, MAX_NON_TURBO_LIM_RATIO, is replayed separately by legacy-intel-platform.py. No original process, driver or hardware is executed.
findings: Scalar read masks 10 bits; indexed read and setter use 11. CPU/firmware binding and physical units remain unresolved.
Scalar setter ORs data with 800003ff, then overwrites MSR 601 with 1fff without verification.
Topology command 80000004 returns three 4-bit addresses and flags. Indexed operations ignore these flags.
Indexed query/write words contain address<<8 and 16/17, but omit bit 31. Input indexes are range checked.
Indexed setters preserve unrelated data bits but ignore errors and only poll completion, with no readback comparison.
Topology and setters can poll indefinitely. Indexed reader has a bounded poll count but returns payload even when still busy or failed.
The reader returns three raw 11-bit values and appends three bit-31 flags to the supplied bool vector.
These behaviors characterize legacy instructions, not a validated platform protocol or enabled GUI/CLI controls.
supplemental_local_research.validation: Local Python/Unicorn execution, not included in the bc30c4f cloud-source snapshot
